lessons.problemPattern: Rules are grouped by nearby entity or chapter instead of the question each rule answers.
decisionLogic: Who is affected maps to target selection.
How an action is executed maps to action mode or direction.
When it starts maps to trigger; how often maps to interval; how far maps to range; the outcome maps to damage or effect.

lessons.problemPattern: A lifecycle template either hides missing stages or invents unsupported stages and low-value final questions.
decisionLogic: Check existence, entry, persistent behavior, interaction, state change, death, exit, and removal only when applicable.
Create rules only for supported stages and distinguish internal closure semantics from player-facing planning decisions.

lessons.problemPattern: A persistent state is treated as constant because analysis focuses on isolated events or frames.
decisionLogic: Compare the same eligible state property across bounded time windows.
Visual change creates an unreviewed candidate; it cannot become a configured rule or published fact without review.

lessons.problemPattern: Observed values, patterns, randomness, and hidden parameters are promoted into stronger rules without evidence.
decisionLogic: Keep observed value, inferred pattern, configured value, explicit formula, and unknown distinct.
Random observation does not imply equal probability, replacement mode, weight, priority, or guarantee.

lessons.problemPattern: Heterogeneous selectable objects are collapsed into a generic candidate pool and assumed to share rules.
decisionLogic: Resolve candidate types before rendering a candidate mechanism.
Do not share eligibility, sampling, weight, capacity, or limits across types without explicit evidence.

lessons.problemPattern: The same semantic rule is fully defined in multiple chapters or reported missing before approved information is searched globally.
decisionLogic: Assign one canonical full definition and render other uses as references or summaries.
Before opening a closure gap, search all approved information for the same semantic responsibility.

lessons.problemPattern: A missing structured rule is mistaken for an unknown project rule even when confirmed narrative contains the rule.
decisionLogic: Search confirmed overview, basic flow, chapter summaries, approved facts, approved rules, and planner-confirmed feedback.
Unreviewed narrative cannot become a project fact or close a required slot.

lessons.problemPattern: A recovered rule is considered complete while its referenced entity, state, result, or mechanic remains undefined.
decisionLogic: Resolve every referenced entity, state, result, and mechanic to an approved definition or a concrete applicable gap.
Do not publish dangling mechanic references.

lessons.problemPattern: Logically inevitable consequences with no additional execution value pollute the final planning document.
decisionLogic: Decompose composite rules into atomic clauses and classify execution, player-visible, exception, trivial, and redundant value.
Suppress trivial and redundant clauses while preserving explicit exceptions.

lessons.problemPattern: A value observed in one run is promoted into a general gameplay rule or configuration.
decisionLogic: Keep single-run values as run-scoped evidence by default.
Publish a general rule only when configuration, repeated evidence, explicit formula, or planner confirmation supplies general authority.

lessons.problemPattern: Atomic rules are rendered in creation or evidence order instead of mechanic semantics and execution order.
decisionLogic: Group rules by semantic responsibility before rendering.
Order selection mechanics as trigger, state entry, generation, type resolution, selection, effect, exit, refresh, and numeric examples.

lessons.problemPattern: A static screenshot is treated as proof that the game or player is in a static no-action state.
decisionLogic: The input medium describes available evidence, not player behavior or game state.

When a screenshot cannot prove an operation, keep the player action unknown and create a planner decision card with explicit operation choices and a custom answer; never publish no-action as a conclusion.
Only describe a static display state when the game content itself explicitly supports that state.

lessons.problemPattern: A confirmed chapter directory is mistaken for completed gameplay content, so downstream review and export show polished headings with empty or screenshot-caption bodies.
decisionLogic: Directory confirmation proves information architecture only; it does not prove that detailed rules exist.
P4 through P7 require a detailed gameplay model or an explicitly preserved last valid detailed revision.
When detailed generation fails, preserve the confirmed directory, expose the exact failure and retry action, and never export the skeleton as a document.

Long-running chapter generation must expose determinate progress and the latest safe milestone; timeout measures continuous inactivity rather than total elapsed work so a large valid directory is not killed while chapters are still completing.

lessons.problemPattern: Screenshot page names, UI labels, duplicate nouns and unrelated template concepts are flattened into gameplay chapters or one oversized subsystem.
decisionLogic: Build the directory as gameplay system to subsystem to independently auditable mechanism, with distinct names at every level.
Treat pages, panels, popups, display states and buttons as evidence or interaction artifacts, never as gameplay mechanisms by themselves.
Reject duplicate mechanisms and split an overloaded subsystem by real business responsibility before asking the planner to review it.
Isolate generation cache by project and summarize structure only from the current project's accepted hierarchy.

lessons.problemPattern: Static evidence, numeric facts and presentation rules are treated as gameplay flow, while cached or recovered model data can cross task boundaries.
decisionLogic: Route approved rules by semantic responsibility before rendering: flow and interaction may enter gameplay flow, while presentation, numeric and configuration rules keep separate owners.
A declared flow must contain a causal initiation and outcome; static UI evidence or a current value alone cannot satisfy that contract.
Store structure quality and detailed semantic quality separately, and block downstream review whenever detailed quality explicitly fails.
Apply the same validator to every task and isolate models and caches by task identity, evidence or interaction revision, and approved gameplay revision.
